summary: Two tables in the same issues carry the exact title 'Sales and Redemptions by Periods, All Series Combined'. One sits in the UNITED STATES SAVINGS BONDS section, the other in the TREASURY SAVINGS NOTES section. The question's parenthetical '(U.S. Treasury)' is ambiguous between them. c (right) treated it as a generic source label, used the savings-bonds table's Sales column for CY1949-1953, checked the latest printing that still carries CY1949, and computed the mean with calc. a read '(U.S. Treasury)' as pointing to Treasury savings notes and used the notes table's latest (1956_08) values, including one revised year. Its mean came out about 0.4% high. a then repeated one identical show_table command 40 times until Codex auto-compacted the context, and answered from the compaction summary. b actually computed the savings-bonds mean with calc, the same value c submitted. It submitted that as --answer, with the Treasury-notes mean as --alt. The competing_candidates rule echoed the alt back as 'Offer'. b read the Offer as a harness-computed correction and accepted it, so its final answer was a value it had worked out in its head, with an arithmetic slip (about 0.2% high, and not even the correct notes-table mean). The gate turned a right answer into a wrong one.

first_divergence.where: b item_26 (finds the two same-title tables), item_44 (savings-bonds latest values), item_48 (mental mean for the notes table after the 1956_08 revision, with an arithmetic slip), item_64 (calc on savings-bonds values), item_65 (submit --answer <bonds mean> --alt <notes mean>), item_66-item_67 (reads the Offer as harness advice and accepts); a item_55-item_56, item_60, item_66
first_divergence.what_b_did: Chose the savings-bonds table as its primary answer, grounded in calc, but also passed the Treasury-notes reading as --alt. That alt was computed in b's reasoning, not in calc, and the arithmetic was wrong. When the gate offered the alt back, b accepted it.
first_divergence.what_a_did: Chose the Treasury-notes table outright ('The wording points to the Treasury savings notes table'), took the latest 1956_08 printing and computed the mean with calc, then looped.

seed_text_effect.which_advice: Unless the question names a publication date or issue, use the latest printing of each value
seed_text_effect.evidence: In item_61-item_62 a spotted that one notes-table year was revised in the 1956_08 printing and used the revised value (item_62 printings --years 1956-1956). a ignored the seed's loop advice: items 70-146 are the same show_table command repeated 40 times. The seed's 'Alternatives ... weigh them against the question's exact wording and answer the one it asks for' did not stop a from picking the less likely table.

mechanism_effect.workflow_cost: The gate was decisive and harmful. Round 1: competing_candidates showed 'Offer: <alt> (your --alt)' plus a one-line Accept command, while Keep required writing a reason. b's mech SEED.md says an Offer means the harness 'computed that alternative itself, from your own calculation with one input replaced'. For competing_candidates that is false: the offer is just the model's own --alt echoed back. b's next note shows it took the claim literally: 'Harness says offer alt computed from own calculation with input replaced. It suggests maybe correct is [alt]... We can accept.' Round 2: recompute_final fired, because the accepted value was never output by any calc run. The check trace records it as fired, but it was suppressed (state_before offered=true), so the answer was recorded unchecked. The protocol therefore promoted an unverified, mis-computed alternative and then switched off the one rule that would have caught it.

tools_usage.a: find_tables x6+; show_table on the 1954_12 bonds table; printings by title (merged both same-title tables into one SUMMARY); guessed table ids (SB-2, USB-2, ...); read the .harness wrapper; rg/sed of raw pages; show_table 1956_08 on the notes table; printings --years 1956; calc. Then 40 identical show_table calls at a line that resolves to the Series E-K table, which a had already rejected.
tools_usage.b: find_tables x6; rg over the 1950s corpus; sed of raw pages to tell the two same-title tables apart; show_table on the 1954_12 notes table; printings by title (merged tables); a detour into capital-movements tables; calc for the bonds mean only; submit with --alt; then Accept.

first_divergence.where: a item_55-item_56 (decides the parenthetical means Treasury savings notes) and item_60 (show_table on the notes table in 1956_08); c item_11 (show_table on the 1954_12 savings-bonds table), item_21 and item_37 (reasons that 'U.S. Treasury' is a generic source label and 'all series combined' refers to savings bonds), item_51 (sed on the 1955_12 bonds table to confirm the latest CY1949 printing), item_53 calc
first_divergence.what_c_did: Used the savings-bonds 'All Series Combined' table's Sales column (not 'Sales plus accrued discount') for CY1949-1953, checked the latest printing of each, and computed the mean with calc.
first_divergence.what_a_did: Used the same-titled Treasury savings notes table's Sales column at its last (1956_08) printing, giving a mean about 0.4% high.

c_vs_a.temperature_effect: Each cell weighed both readings of '(U.S. Treasury)' and landed on opposite sides: c at item_15 and item_37, a at item_38-item_46 and item_55. Sampling plausibly decided this coin-flip. T=0 also produced a degenerate repetition: a re-issued the identical command 40 times (items 70-146) until auto-compaction, stretching the run to about 604 s, 74 requests and 7.8M input tokens, against c's 209 s and 27 requests. The loop did not change a's answer, which was already computed at item_66, but it used up the budget without any re-examination of the table choice.

lesson: The mechanism's Accept/Keep protocol is actively harmful when an Offer is only the model's own --alt. The seed wording ('the harness computed that alternative itself') gives that echo a false authority, and the one-line Accept makes deferring the easy path. Four fixes follow. First, do not attach an Offer to competing_candidates. Second, never let an accepted offer bypass recompute_final or grounded. Third, reword the seed so it describes an Offer as a candidate, not a correction. Fourth, discourage --alt unless the alt came from calc. On discovery: when two tables share a title, find_tables/show_table should print the section heading prominently and printings should not merge them, since both a's and b's confusion started from merged SUMMARY output. T=0 needs an external loop breaker, because the seed's loop advice did not stop a 40x repeat in the text arm, and only the mech arm had broker loop notes.
